tasks.title: Keep the pressed button distinct from hover in every palette
tasks.description: Moved on 2026-09-25 from themes follow-up 23 (PRESS-DISTINCT), found in the IE-D3 review. The shared button helper's pressed fill turns a panel into `selected` and its hover fill into `hover` (`Palette::control_fill`, crates/app/src/appearance.rs), so on every surface pressed stands only as far from hover as the palette's own `selected` stands from `hover`. Measured: Sandstone is 3 per channel apart (eddfd0 against eae1d3, 1.009:1) on every surface; Porcelain is 6 per channel apart, 4 over the hovered selected row; Kanagawa Wave's `selected` (24364e) is darker than its `hover` (363646), so pressed differs from hover by hue rather than a further lift. No readability rule checks this pair, and the button test's floor CONTROL_PRESS_DISTANCE (3) is Sandstone's value. Proposed rule: `selected` differs from `hover` by at least 8 in one channel and sits at least as far from `panel` as `hover` in the lift direction. Margin limit: Solarized Dark's button label is 4.575:1 on the pressed fill over the hovered selected row, which clears 4.5 but not its 0.25 margin, and reaching the margin would move its label off `text`. Non-blocking notes from the same review: in a custom theme whose `hover` moves a channel toward 0 or 255 from a panel already near that end, the fill's opacity approaches 1 and the hover disappears on hovered rows, and the same holds for `selected` and pressed; in Kanagawa Lotus and One Dark a disabled selected helper is transparent over its surface while the other 18 themes keep a subtle chip (the command palette's disabled Open command). Changing a built-in palette changes its committed themes frames, so recapture them against a same-session base.

acceptance.description: The readability rules in docs/development/themes/spec.md state the selected-versus-hover rule (the proposed one or a justified variant), and `readability_issues` (crates/app/src/appearance/custom.rs) reports a palette that breaks it, with a unit test that fails on the unchanged Sandstone palette.

Sandstone, Porcelain and Kanagawa Wave meet the rule or are explicitly exempted, with the reason recorded in spec.md and in the test; every other built-in theme still passes the full readability rule set.

CONTROL_PRESS_DISTANCE in the shared button test is raised to the rule's distance, and appearance::tests::shared_button_fills_lift_every_surface_and_keep_the_label_readable passes for every built-in theme.

Native captures on Linux X11 at scale factor 1 show hover and pressed on a row action, a header button and the Stage button in each tuned theme against a same-session base. Committed frames of tuned palettes under docs/evidence/themes/ and docs/evidence/button-states/ are recaptured, a design review rules on every non-timing difference, and a dated docs/validation.md entry records which frames changed and why.

tasks.title: Warm the Arch Linux container job with a trusted Rust cache
tasks.description: Owner request of 2026-09-29. `Rust tests · archlinux` is cold on every run: 15m43s to 15m47s in quality runs 36599383720, 36608513381, 36618045403, 36620122201 and 36622842027. The warm Ubuntu and macOS test jobs took 3m13s to 5m47s in the same runs whenever their caches hit, so Arch decides when a product pull request goes green. Setup is not the cost: in run 36622842027, container start took 16 s, the pacman upgrade and install 10 s, and the toolchain 6 s. The nextest step took 902 s, almost all of it compiling the whole dependency graph. The lever is a build cache. docs/ci.md ("No cache") explains why there is none yet. The setup action keys native identity on `dpkg-query`, which does not exist in the container. A key over the full pacman inventory would churn with nearly every Arch update and evict the Ubuntu and macOS entries from the 10 GB repository quota. And no pull request may write an entry that `main` trusts. Design a key over the inputs that actually change compiled output. Keep Arch's rolling-release coverage. Measure the result on hosted runs. Source and local checks are not enough: this needs hosted cold and warm runs.

acceptance.description: The Arch job restores and saves a Rust build cache. The key names the target and the pinned toolchain (`rustc -vV`), the lockfile and manifests, `vendor/` contents, the profile and flags, and the Arch native inputs that reach compiled output: at least the C compiler, glibc and the linked native libraries' versions, not the whole pacman inventory. `scripts/ci` tests show that changing each keyed input gives a new key and a rebuild. A hit never skips a build or test step. A missing or corrupt cache falls back to a correct cold run.

Only pushes to `main` save the Arch entry; pull requests restore it and never write an entry that `main` restores. The entry's size and retention are bounded. docs/ci.md records its size and the repository's cache total against the 10 GB limit, and shows the Ubuntu and macOS entries are not evicted continuously. The job still runs as the unprivileged `builder` account, and no credential is stored.

Every run still upgrades to that day's Arch packages behind the unchanged pacman signature check, and prints the package versions. A change in a keyed native input invalidates the cache instead of reusing objects built against the old libraries.

A dated record under docs/benchmarks/ gives the Arch job's duration and its nextest step's, cold and warm, before and after, with run IDs, hit or miss, restore and save times, and the entry size. On a warm pull-request run with the lockfile, `vendor/` and the toolchain unchanged, the Arch job finishes within 2 minutes of the slowest warm `Rust tests and Clippy` job of the same run, and its `--timings` show the dependencies fresh.

docs/ci.md's Arch section describes the mechanism, the key and its invalidation, replacing the "No cache" and "Cost" paragraphs. The workflow passes the repository's Actions lint and `scripts/ci` test suite. Action revisions stay pinned by commit.

tasks.title: Report disabled Buttons as disabled to AT-SPI on Linux
tasks.description: Hard; investigate before editing. Owner request of 2026-09-30. Queued in docs/development/queue-2026-09-30.json, a self-contained queue with no dependency into tasks.json. Interactive: if it vendors a crate it needs a row in vendor/AGENTS.md, which the unattended controller refuses to change (runner.py `controlled`). Run it in an interactive session, and stop an unattended run before it becomes eligible; it is last in the chain. On Linux every disabled Button reports `enabled` and `sensitive` to AT-SPI (docs/validation.md "September 30 Tab leaves a focused Button that turns disabled", Accessibility), and docs/native-accessibility.md:19 qualifies its claim. The cause is the pinned `accesskit_atspi_common` 0.19.1: `src/node.rs:373-377` adds `Enabled|Sensitive` unless the role supports read-only and the node is read-only or disabled, and `accesskit_consumer` 0.38.0 `is_read_only_supported` (`src/node.rs:844`) excludes Button. So gpui-base's `set_disabled()` (vendor/gpui-base/src/button.rs:332) never reaches AT-SPI. Planner research, checked 2026-09-30 on crates.io and in the published crates: AccessKit fixed this in accesskit_atspi_common 0.21.0 (2026-09-25; "Expose non-disabled nodes as enabled and sensitive on Unix", AccessKit/accesskit#788, commit 6ee0558b, +6/-4 in adapters/atspi-common/src/node.rs). 0.21.0 needs accesskit 0.25 and accesskit_consumer 0.39, and accesskit_unix 0.24.0 carries it. The workspace pins accesskit 0.24.1 and accesskit_unix 0.22.1 through gpui-pre-linux 0.3.4. Even gpui-pre-linux 0.3.7 (2026-09-28; gpui-kit 0.7.0 pins gpui-pre =0.3.7) still requires `accesskit ^0.24` and `accesskit_unix ^0.22`, so no compatible release carries the fix. accesskit_consumer 0.38.0 already has the `is_read_only()` (node.rs:452) the fix calls. Options: (a) vendor accesskit_atspi_common 0.19.1 (MIT OR Apache-2.0) with the #788 backport through `[patch.crates-io]`, like the four existing vendor patches; (b) ask upstream for a 0.19.x backport release, which only the owner can do; (c) wait for a gpui-pre release on accesskit 0.25. The planner favours (a), with (b) in parallel; re-check these facts first. A dependency change needs the independent security review (docs/development/security-review.md), license and advisory checks and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. deny.toml is a policy file and stays out of scope. Not covered: VoiceOver on macOS, which this Linux host cannot reach (the macOS adapter is untouched), Orca speech and Windows. Last in the queue and chain: it is the hardest and needs an owner decision on a new vendored crate.

acceptance.description: A dated note, docs/development/YYYY-MM-DD-accesskit-atspi-disabled.md, follows docs/development/research-template.md. It re-checks the versions and the upstream fix above against crates.io and the AccessKit repository at a pinned revision, compares options (a) to (c), and states the recommendation and its removal condition. The pull request follows the note, or stops at it if the note recommends leaving dependencies unchanged for now.

Under option (a), vendor/accesskit_atspi_common holds the 0.19.1 source with only the #788 change applied. A `[patch.crates-io]` entry selects it, and the workspace excludes it like the other vendor patches. Its GITTURTLE-PATCH.md records the upstream crate version and checksum, the upstream commit, the modified file, the consuming path (gpui-pre-linux, then accesskit_unix, then this crate) and the removal condition (a gpui-pre release on accesskit_unix 0.24 or later). vendor/AGENTS.md's table, Cargo.lock and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md are updated, and `cargo deny --locked check` passes.

A test fails without the backport and passes with it. It maps an AccessKit tree with a disabled and an enabled Button, a disabled Switch and a disabled CheckBox through the adapter's state set. Disabled nodes carry none of Enabled, Sensitive or ReadOnly, and enabled ones keep Enabled and Sensitive. Vendored crates are excluded workspace members, so the test runs either with `--manifest-path` or as a Linux-only app test; its command is recorded.

A native AT-SPI read on Linux X11 at scale factor 1, base and candidate in the same session, with `qa.py identity` on both and input through Mutter RemoteDesktop with verified X focus on this GNOME host (never XTest). `org.a11y.Status IsEnabled` is set for those launches only and read back afterwards. Enabled Buttons keep their states, and Targets' focused disabled Switch button keeps `focusable` and `focused`. Any committed frame is privacy-scanned. docs/native-accessibility.md:19 and a new dated docs/validation.md entry say what changed and name VoiceOver on macOS and Orca speech as not covered.
`python3 scripts/gate.py full --base origin/main` passes, and the independent security review of the dependency change passes.
